title: Decision queue: verify and update for stream-json transport
description:
The decision queue (Pane 3) was delivered in bp6-pdr.4 against the PTY transport. With stream-json, poe:decision events arrive via the 'poe-decision-queued' Tauri event. Must be verified and updated end-to-end.

Verify/fix frontend:
1. Queue panel receives and displays poe:decision items from 'poe-decision-queued' Tauri event
2. Human resolution calls invoke('resolve_queue_item', {item_id, project_id, resolution})
   [actual command name — NOT resolve_decision]
3. Queue item clears after resolution

Rust-side work required — resolve_queue_item must be extended (currently only writes to SQLite):
- After writing resolution: emit 'poe-decision-resolved' Tauri event with the resolved QueueItem
- Send DagChanged::NodeStatusChanged to dag_tx so the orchestrator processes the resolved task
- Orchestrator resumes the waiting agent: spawn_agent with resume_session_id = task's agent session_id
  and a bundle containing 'Human: {resolution}' as the prompt content
- CRITICAL cwd constraint (Protocol.md §5): the --resume spawn MUST use project.path as cwd;
  a cwd mismatch causes Claude to return 'No conversation found with session ID'

Verify end-to-end:
4. Queue item clears after 'poe-decision-resolved' fires
5. Agent receives resolution and continues (visible in activity feed as new poe:step/poe:done events)

This is a core Phase 2 deliverable. Without a working queue, human oversight does not function.

Conversational thread mode (multi-round poe:decision) is Phase 3 (bp6-7ct.7) — not in scope here.
notes:
DEEPER THAN STATED — three pre-existing bugs plus a missing orchestrator path must be fixed end-to-end.

BUG 1 — handle_decision doesn't set task status to waiting (event_ingester/mod.rs):
Protocol.md §2 requires poe:decision → UPDATE tasks.status=waiting. handle_decision only creates the queue item and emits poe-decision-queued. Task remains 'running'. Fix: add db_update_node call setting status=Waiting inside handle_decision.

BUG 2 — handle_done overwrites waiting with Complete (event_ingester/mod.rs):
Agent emits poe:decision then poe:done (exits). handle_done unconditionally sets status=Complete. So after both events, task is Complete — not waiting. Orchestrator advances dependents incorrectly. Fix: handle_done must check for unresolved queue items (db_count_unresolved_queue_items) before setting Complete. If unresolved items exist, set status=Waiting, not Complete.

BUG 3 — NodeStatus::Waiting may not exist:
types.ts declares status: 'pending'|'running'|'blocked'|'complete'|'cancelled' — no 'waiting'. Check dag_store/types.rs for NodeStatus enum and add Waiting variant if absent. Add to TypeScript types. Update poe-node-updated handling in usePoeProject.ts to handle this status.

MISSING ORCHESTRATOR PATH — QueueItemResolved doesn't trigger resume:
DagChanged::QueueItemResolved variant exists (event_ingester/mod.rs line 15) and signal_project_id routes it. But run_loop only finds pending tasks — it has no branch for 'resume waiting agent after decision'. This path must be written:

In orchestrator/mod.rs, add a handle_queue_item_resolved path triggered when DagChanged::QueueItemResolved is received:
1. Look up the QueueItem from SQLite by item_id to get task_id and resolution
2. Look up the task's session_id from the agents table (most recent completed agent for task_id)
3. Assemble resume bundle: '---\nHuman: {resolution}' (Protocol.md §5 format)
4. Call spawn_agent with resume_session_id = session_id, input_bundle = resolution bundle
5. Set task status back to Running before spawn

All spawns in this path MUST use project.path as cwd (same constraint as handover — cwd mismatch causes 'No conversation found with session ID').

title: Agent interrupt controls: task cancel, stage pause, project abort
description:
Add interrupt controls per UX-Brief.

Three levels, all accessible from the project header.

IMPORTANT: cancel_node in dag_store/commands.rs is DB-only (calls db_cancel_node which sets status=Cancelled).
It does NOT send SIGTERM. SIGTERM requires AgentMap access (agent_lifecycle::AgentMap).
All three interrupt commands below must live in orchestrator/commands.rs where AgentMap state is accessible,
not dag_store/commands.rs.

1. Task cancel:
   - Confirm modal: 'Cancel task X? The agent will be stopped.'
   - New or augmented command: cancel_task(node_id, project_id) in orchestrator/commands.rs
   - Rust: look up agent in AgentMap by task_id, send SIGTERM via interrupt_agent_process(),
     then call db_cancel_node() to update status. (cancel_node in dag_store can remain for
     DB-only use cases but is not sufficient here.)

2. Stage pause (new command):
   - Confirm modal: 'Pause stage? N agents will be stopped. Tasks will re-queue.'
   - invoke('pause_stage', {project_id, phase_id}) -> ()
   - Rust: SIGTERM all agents in AgentMap whose task belongs to phase_id,
     set their tasks = Pending, set phase status = Paused

3. Project abort (new command):
   - Confirm modal: 'Abort project? N agents running across M tasks will be stopped.'
   - invoke('abort_project', {project_id}) -> ()
   - Rust: SIGTERM all agents in AgentMap for this project_id,
     all Running tasks -> Pending, project status = Paused

On resume after pause/abort: orchestrator attempts --resume for all previously-running tasks
using stored session_ids. 'Resume' button appears in project header when project/stage is Paused.
notes:
CORRECTION on cancel_node: the existing cancel_node command in dag_store/commands.rs calls db_cancel_node which only updates node status in SQLite. It does NOT send SIGTERM to the agent process. There is no AgentMap access in dag_store/commands.rs.

The SIGTERM capability exists as interrupt_agent_process() in agent_lifecycle/mod.rs (lines 377-397) — it takes AgentMap and agent_id and sends SIGTERM via kill. But it is not called by cancel_node.

For task cancel to actually stop a running agent, the implementation must either:
(a) Add a new cancel_task command in orchestrator/commands.rs (which can access both AgentMap and ProjectRegistry via Tauri State), or
(b) Augment the existing cancel_node by moving it to orchestrator/commands.rs and adding AgentMap access.

All three interrupt commands (cancel, pause_stage, abort_project) require AgentMap access and belong in orchestrator/commands.rs. For cancel: look up agent_id by task_id in AgentMap, call interrupt_agent_process, then db_cancel_node. For pause_stage and abort_project: iterate AgentMap entries filtered by project/phase, call interrupt_agent_process for each, update task statuses in SQLite.

title: Agent session handover panel: xterm.js + WebSocket
description:
New frontend component: AgentHandover panel (poe2/src/).

Triggered by clicking an activity feed entry or a 'Handover' button on a task detail panel.

Frontend behaviour:
1. invoke('agent_handover_open', {node_id}) -> ws_port
2. Connect xterm.js to ws://127.0.0.1:{ws_port}
3. FitAddon to fill available space; send {type:'resize', cols, rows} on connect and window resize
4. Forward keyboard input as WS Binary messages
5. On WS close: show '[session ended]' in terminal; on panel close: invoke('agent_handover_close', {node_id})

Header: 'claude --resume <session_id>' label, skill name, task title.
Distinct from project terminal (tmux). Both coexist as separate panels.

Rust fixes required in pty_handover.rs (three known bugs):

1. cwd bug (critical — must fix):
   CommandBuilder::new('claude') at line ~105 has no .cwd() call.
   Protocol.md §5 documents that Claude scopes sessions by project directory —
   --resume with a mismatched cwd returns 'No conversation found with session ID'.
   Fix: while iterating reg.values() to find the session_id, also capture db.project.path,
   then call cmd.cwd(project_path) before spawning.

2. Keyboard input TODO (in scope for 2.2 — must resolve):
   Lines 196-199 have an explicit TODO comment: keyboard input is received from WS
   but dropped (the write path is not wired). The handover panel is read-only until this is fixed.
   Fix requires storing a cloneable PTY writer reference in HandoverSession — see the TODO comment
   for context. Decide: fix in 2.2 or defer to 2.3 and document explicitly in the bead.

3. Session lookup scope:
   Line 63 query: WHERE status = 'running'. This means handover fails for recently-completed agents
   whose --resume session is still valid.
   Consider widening to: status IN ('running', 'complete') ordered by started_at DESC.
   If deferred, the panel's 'Handover' button should only appear on running tasks.
notes:
Three pre-existing Rust bugs must be fixed as part of this task (in addition to writing the React component):

BUG 1 — cwd not set (CRITICAL, Protocol.md §5):
In agent/pty_handover.rs, CommandBuilder::new('claude') has no .cwd() call. The PTY process inherits the app's working directory, not the project path. Claude scopes sessions by directory — a mismatch causes 'No conversation found with session ID'. Fix: cmd.cwd(&project_path), where project_path is looked up from the project record alongside session_id.

BUG 2 — Keyboard input TODO (read-only session):
pty_handover.rs lines 196-202 have an explicit TODO comment: 'wire keyboard input properly'. The WS→PTY keyboard path currently discards all Binary messages. The handover panel is currently read-only. Fix: store a separate Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn Write + Send>>> writer in HandoverSession and write Binary WS messages to it.

BUG 3 — Session query too narrow:
agent_handover_open queries 'WHERE status = running'. The UX-Brief says clicking any activity feed entry opens the handover, including entries from completed agents whose sessions are still resumable. Fix: remove the status filter or use 'ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 1' across all statuses, so recently-finished agents can also be inspected.

description:

title: Create agent/transport.rs — JsonStreamTransport
description:
New module: poe2/src-tauri/src/agent/transport.rs

Responsibility: spawn Claude with stream-json, write the input bundle to stdin, read and parse the JSON output stream. Nothing else.

Public interface:
  struct JsonStreamTransport
  fn run(bundle: &str, resume_session_id: Option<&str>, cwd: &Path, callbacks: StreamCallbacks) -> Result<()>

  struct StreamCallbacks {
    on_session_id: Box<dyn Fn(String)>,          // fires once on init event
    on_text_chunk: Box<dyn Fn(String)>,          // fires for each text chunk from assistant events
    on_raw_json: Box<dyn Fn(serde_json::Value)>, // fires for every JSON object (for logging)
    on_complete: Box<dyn Fn()>,                  // fires when result event received
  }

Invocation:
  claude --output-format stream-json --verbose -p --dangerously-skip-permissions [--resume <id>]
  env: CLAUDECODE removed
  stdin: write bundle bytes then drop (EOF)
  stdout: read newline-delimited JSON

Session ID extracted from {type:system, subtype:init} event; delivered via on_session_id before any text callbacks.

Does not know about SQLite, Tauri, orchestration, or poe: events. Pure process I/O only.
notes: on_text_chunk fires on: (1) assistant events with content[].type==text, (2) content_block_delta events with delta.type==text_delta. See Protocol.md §5.

title: Create agent/text_extractor.rs — TextBufExtractor
description:
New module: poe2/src-tauri/src/agent/text_extractor.rs

Responsibility: accumulate text from stream-json assistant events and yield complete lines for poe: parsing. Nothing else.

pub struct TextBufExtractor {
    buf: String,
}
impl TextBufExtractor {
    pub fn push(&mut self, text: &str) -> Vec<String>  // returns complete lines
    pub fn flush(&mut self) -> Option<String>           // tail — no trailing newline
}

Input: raw text strings from JsonStreamTransport's on_poe_line callback.
Output: complete text lines, one at a time, ready for event_ingester::parse_poe_event.

No ANSI stripping. No JSON parsing. No SQLite. No Tauri.
This is the only place the text accumulation concern lives.

Unit-testable in isolation: construct TextBufExtractor, push strings, assert lines returned.

title: POE Attempt 2 — Phase 2.1: Refactor Protocol
description:
Replace the PTY-based agent spawn with the stream-json transport proven by stdio_json_harness and session_handoff_harness. Strict single-responsibility architecture: each protocol concern (transport, event extraction, ingestion, PTY handover) lives in its own module. No protocol parsing may bleed into orchestration or UI layers.

Foundational decisions (see doc-POE/Protocol.md §5):
- Primary transport: claude --output-format stream-json -p --dangerously-skip-permissions
- Session ID from {type:system,subtype:init,session_id:...} JSON event
- poe: events extracted from assistant text via text_buf accumulation (no ANSI stripping)
- Decision/review continuation via --resume into a new stream-json session
- Human handover: claude --resume via PTY + xterm.js WebSocket bridge
- Skill mode injection: autonomous vs interactive block prepended at bundle assembly

This phase is a prerequisite for Phase 2.2 (UX refactor) which depends on the new Tauri commands defined here.

title: test: Rust integration test harness for poe: protocol against Claude
description:
Build a deterministic Rust integration test that validates the full protocol path — from bundle injection through PTY to poe: event parsing — using the real orchestrator code.

PURPOSE:
Before fixing bp6-pdr.13 (PTY column width) and bp6-pdr.14 (decision resolution), we need a repeatable way to observe what Claude actually emits through the PTY and confirm the parser receives it correctly. This harness is that instrument.

TEST DESIGN:
Not agent-driven. A deterministic test binary (or cargo integration test) that:
1. Spawns Claude via the same PTY mechanism as agent_lifecycle::spawn_agent
2. Injects a fixed, minimal skill bundle designed to produce a known, predictable output
3. Captures all PTY output lines
4. Runs each line through event_ingester::ingest_line (the real production parser)
5. Asserts expected poe: events were received, in order, with correct field values
6. Fails clearly if events are missing, malformed, or out of order

SKILL BUNDLE FOR TESTING:
Use a minimal test skill that instructs Claude to emit a fixed, short sequence of poe: events with no ambiguity. Example:
- poe:brief with a known content string
- poe:step with a known name
- poe:artifact with a short, known content field (e.g. 200 chars) AND a long content field (e.g. 5KB) — to expose the PTY line-wrap bug
- poe:done

The skill must be written to emit these events with no variation — pure protocol compliance test, not a realistic CONOPS run.

THINGS TO ASSERT:
- All events received (none silently dropped)
- JSON parses cleanly (no ANSI pollution or line-wrap fragments)
- poe:artifact content field is intact (not truncated at 220 chars)
- Event ordering matches emission order
- poe:done is the final event

THINGS TO CAPTURE FOR DIAGNOSTICS:
- All raw PTY lines (before parsing) — logged to test output so failures are debuggable
- Which lines were recognised as poe: events vs ignored as raw output
- Exact JSON received for each event

INFRASTRUCTURE:
- Lives in poe2/src-tauri/tests/ as a Rust integration test, or as a standalone binary in poe2/src-tauri/src/bin/
- Uses the same portable_pty, event_ingester, and skills modules as production
- Requires claude binary on PATH — skip gracefully if not present (CI-safe)
- Runs with: cargo test --test protocol_harness or cargo run --bin poe-test

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
- Test passes end-to-end on a clean run with no known bugs present
- Test fails deterministically when PTY col width bug (bp6-pdr.13) is present
- Test fails deterministically when ANSI stripping is needed
- Test can be run by a human to verify fixes before marking bp6-pdr.13 and bp6-pdr.14 closed
design:
## Implementation Plan

### Files to modify

**`poe2/src-tauri/src/event_ingester/mod.rs`**
Extract a public pure parsing function with no Tauri or SQLite dependencies:
```rust
pub fn parse_poe_event(line: &str) -> Option<(String, serde_json::Value)>
```
Returns (event_type, full_json_value) if the line is a valid poe: event. `ingest_line` is refactored to call `parse_poe_event` internally — no behaviour change externally.

**`poe2/src-tauri/src/agent_lifecycle/mod.rs`**
Add a protocol-level runner that fully encapsulates PTY setup, TUI-ready detection, and bundle submission:
```rust
pub fn run_agent_capturing(bundle: &str, cwd: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>>
```
Internally: opens PTY at 220 cols × 50 rows, spawns `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`, watches for ⏵ (U+23F5) in output before writing bundle + \r, collects all lines until EOF. TUI-ready wait is entirely internal — callers (including the test harness) have no knowledge of the signal mechanism.

### New files

**`poe2/src-tauri/tests/protocol_harness.rs`**
Cargo integration test. Test skill is embedded as a string constant (not a separate file per design decision).

Test structure:
1. Skip gracefully if `claude` not on PATH (CI-safe)
2. Assemble bundle from embedded TEST_SKILL + fixed task section
3. Call `agent_lifecycle::run_agent_capturing(bundle, tmp_dir)`
4. Log ALL raw PTY lines to test output (always — for debuggability on failure)
5. Run each line through `event_ingester::parse_poe_event`
6. Log which lines were recognised as poe: events vs raw output
7. Assert ordered event sequence:
   - `brief` — with non-empty content field
   - `step` with name "short-artifact"
   - `artifact` name="test-short.txt", content intact
   - `step` with name "long-artifact"
   - `artifact` name="test-long.txt", content.len() > 220 ← key assertion: exposes PTY col-width bug (bp6-pdr.13)
   - `done` — last event

The `content.len() > 220` assertion on the long artifact is deliberate. When the PTY column-width bug (bp6-pdr.13) is present, the JSON line wraps at 220 chars, fragmenting the JSON. `parse_poe_event` returns None for both fragments — the artifact event never appears in the parsed list, and the test fails with a clear message showing the raw fragments.

Test skill design (embedded): Instructs Claude to emit exactly the 6 events. Long artifact uses a repeating alphanumeric pattern provided verbatim in the skill for faithful reproduction. Content string ~400 chars — well past the 220-col wrap point.

**`poe2/src-tauri/tests/README.md`**
- How to run (`cargo test --test protocol_harness`)
- What each assertion tests
- How to interpret failure output (raw PTY lines + parsed events)
- Which known bugs each assertion is designed to catch (bp6-pdr.13 for long artifact, bp6-pdr.14 for event ordering)

### No Cargo.toml changes needed
`portable-pty`, `tempfile`, `serde_json`, `anyhow` all already in dependencies.
notes: Scope expanded (2026-03-08): test skill must exercise all 12 event types — brief, step, artifact (short + long), knowledge, decision, task, task:update, task:cancel, edge, edge:remove, done. review is excluded (requires live orchestrator). Each event type must have a parse assertion. Protocol ordering rules (brief=first, done=last) must also be asserted. This is Option A coverage: full wire-format parsing coverage via parse_poe_event. Option B (ingest_line effects layer) is filed separately.

title: fix: PTY column width too narrow — poe:artifact JSON split across lines
description:
The PTY is opened with cols: 220 (agent_lifecycle/mod.rs ~line 88). A poe:artifact event for even a short CONOPS will be 3-20KB of JSON on a single line. When the PTY renders this, it wraps at column 220, injecting actual newlines into the byte stream. BufReader::lines() splits on newlines. Result: the artifact JSON arrives as 50-100 fragments, none of which parse as valid JSON. Every poe:artifact event silently fails.

FIX: Set cols to a value that will never be hit in practice, e.g. 10000. One-line change in openpty() call.

VERIFY: Look at [agent_lifecycle] PTY> log lines during a run — if artifact JSON is chopped into 220-char pieces, confirmed.

FILE: poe2/src-tauri/src/agent_lifecycle/mod.rs

title: refactor: encapsulate all Claude spawning behind a single AgentSpawner
description:
Refactor poe2/src-tauri/src/agent_lifecycle/mod.rs to be the single authoritative place for Claude process spawning, with the correct spawn model from Protocol.md §5.

ROOT BUG TO FIX: The current mod.rs (lines 94-103) spawns Claude with 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p {bundle}'. The -p flag makes Claude single-shot — it exits after one response, silently breaking poe:decision and poe:review (orchestrator writes to stdin after Claude has already exited). This must be removed.

CORRECT SPAWN MODEL (from Protocol.md §5):
1. Spawn: 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions' — no -p, no CLI bundle arg
2. Write the T+S+K input bundle to the PTY stdin pipe immediately after spawn
3. Keep stdin pipe open until agent exits (writer stays alive in AgentMap — dropping it early sends SIGHUP)
4. Read Claude's startup banner from PTY stdout to extract the session ID (format: 'Session ID: <uuid>'); store in nodes.session_id via db_update_node or equivalent. Session ID capture IS in scope for this task.
5. poe:done is sole completion authority — watchdog reads node status from SQLite (already correct in current code, keep it)

INTERFACE SHAPE DECISION: Keep it as a module-level function (spawn_agent), not a new struct or trait. The goal is not a new abstraction but correct implementation + enforced visibility. Enforce via Rust module privacy: CommandBuilder construction and PTY setup are private to agent_lifecycle — nothing outside the module imports portable_pty or constructs a CommandBuilder. All callers use the public spawn_agent function.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (concrete, checkable):
1. No file outside poe2/src-tauri/src/agent_lifecycle/ imports portable_pty or CommandBuilder — verified by grep + cargo check after removing any such imports
2. 'claude -p' does not appear anywhere in the codebase — verified by grep
3. After spawn, nodes.session_id is populated in the DB (not None) — verified by inspecting the DB after a test run
4. The stdin writer is stored in AgentMap and outlives the spawning thread — verified by code review of ownership chain

STDIN PIPE LIFETIME: The writer (pair.master.take_writer()) must remain alive in AgentMap.writer until the process exits. Do not drop it before the watchdog thread completes. Dropping early sends SIGHUP and kills the agent mid-task. This is already correct in the current code (writer stored in ActiveAgent) — do not regress it during refactor.

See Protocol.md §5 for the full spawn model spec.
notes: Readiness assessment (2026-03-07) identified 5 underspecified areas — all resolved above: -p bug named, session ID in scope, function-not-struct interface, concrete AC, stdin lifetime explicit.
close_reason: Spawn model corrected per Protocol.md §5: -p removed, bundle written to stdin, session ID captured from banner. All 4 ACs pass.

title: Rust orchestrator/ingester integration test harness
description:
Build a Rust-only integration test harness that validates the event ingester and orchestrator against realistic poe: event streams — one test case per flow in doc-POE/Flows.md. No Tauri UI required. Tests run via 'cargo test'. Proves that actual skill output (realistic poe: JSON payloads) is interpreted correctly before the UI is built on top.

**Approach**: Rust integration tests in poe2/src-tauri/tests/. Each test creates an in-memory SQLite database, feeds a realistic poe: event JSON stream to the event ingester (as if an agent had emitted it), then asserts SQLite state and the Tauri events that would have been emitted. The claude spawn is mocked — tests supply fixture JSON streams rather than invoking the real claude binary. This keeps tests deterministic and fast.

**Test cases (one per flow):**

1. **SF-1 + SF-2 — Task dispatch and completion**: Create a pending task. Feed the init event (session_id capture) + poe:brief + poe:step + poe:done stream. Assert: nodes.session_id populated, nodes.status transitions pending→running→done, DagChanged triggered, a second pending task with no dependencies is dispatched automatically.

2. **SF-3/SF-4 (decision path)**: Dispatch a task. Feed poe:decision + poe:yield. Assert: decisions row inserted, nodes.yield_reason='decision', nodes.status='waiting', poe://decision emitted. Call resolve_decision. Assert: orchestrator triggers SF-4 resume, continuation bundle is 'Human: {resolution text}'.

3. **SF-3/SF-4 (review path)**: Dispatch a task. Feed poe:review (id=r1, reviewer_skill=senior-engineer) + poe:yield. Assert: reviewer task created (type=plan_review, review_id=r1), dispatched via SF-1, watchdog timer started, requesting task status='waiting', yield_reason='review'. Feed poe:done from reviewer. Assert: SF-4 triggered with ReviewResult bundle containing r1 findings.

4. **SF-3/SF-4 (chat path)**: Dispatch an interactive task. Feed poe:chat (id=c1) + poe:yield. Assert: chat_turns row inserted (id=c1), yield_reason='chat', poe://chat-turn emitted. Call respond_to_chat. Assert: SF-4 resume triggered with 'Human: {response}'.

5. **SF-3/SF-4 (advisor path)**: Dispatch an advisor task. Feed poe:advisor (id=a1) + poe:yield. Assert: advisor_turns row inserted (id=a1), yield_reason='advisor', poe://advisor-turn emitted. Call respond_to_advisor. Assert: SF-4 resume triggered with 'Human: {response}'.

6. **SF-5 — Plan Composer activation**: Call create_phase × 3 (conops, guardrails, execution). Assert all phases status='pending'. Call activate_phase(phase_1_id). Assert: phase_1.status='running', DagChanged triggered, orchestrator dispatches pending tasks in phase 1, phase 2 and 3 remain pending.

7. **Phase gate + advance_phase**: Mark all tasks in a phase as done. Feed poe:done from final task. Assert: orchestrator detects phase complete, sets phases.status='gate', emits poe://phase-update (status: gate). Call advance_phase. Assert: phase_1.status='complete', phase_2.status='running', orchestrator dispatches phase 2 tasks.

8. **Phase gate + revise_phase**: Phase at gate. Call revise_phase(phase_id, task_ids=[t1, t2]). Assert: t1 and t2 reset to pending, t3 (done, not in list) remains done, phase.status='running', orchestrator dispatches t1 and t2 only.

9. **Phase gate + rerun_phase**: Phase at gate. Call rerun_phase(phase_id). Assert: all done tasks in phase reset to pending, phase.status='running', orchestrator dispatches all of them.

10. **skill_modes population**: SF-1 dispatch with a skill file whose frontmatter declares modes: [autonomous, interactive]. Assert: nodes.skill_modes = '["autonomous","interactive"]' written to SQLite at dispatch time.

**Coverage note**: SF-3/SF-4 multi-reviewer variant (parallel reviewers, batched ReviewResult) and the watchdog retry path are covered by sub-cases within test 3.

**Work in**: poe2/src-tauri/tests/ (new integration test file, e.g. orchestrator_flows.rs). Fixture poe: JSON streams in poe2/src-tauri/tests/fixtures/ — realistic payloads matching Protocol.md §2 wire format exactly. No new production code; test infrastructure only.

description: Rust test executables that black-box test the orchestrator and related components for all poe: flows. No agent, no UI — deterministic mock agent output injected via stdin pipe. Tests run as cargo test or standalone CLI executables.
notes:
Acceptance criteria — done when all of the following pass as cargo test or standalone CLI binaries with no real claude process:

SF-1: pending task with valid skill → agent spawned, task status Running
SF-1: pending task with missing skill → task cancelled, error logged
SF-2: agent exits 0 after poe:done → task Done, summary stored
SF-2: agent exits non-0 → task Failed, error logged
SF-3/decision: poe:yield after poe:decision → yield_reason='decision', task Waiting, no auto-resume
SF-3/chat: poe:yield after poe:chat → yield_reason='chat', task Waiting, chat_turns row inserted
SF-3/review: poe:yield after poe:review → yield_reason='review', reviewer task dispatched
SF-3/null: poe:yield with no prior trigger → yield_reason NULL, task Waiting
SF-4/decision single-round: resolve_decision → agent resumed, mock emits poe:done → task Done
SF-4/decision multi-round: resolve_decision → agent resumed, mock emits poe:decision + poe:yield (NOT poe:done) → task back to Waiting; second resolve_decision → resumed again → mock emits poe:done → task Done
SF-4/chat single-round: respond_to_chat → agent resumed, mock emits poe:artifact + poe:done → task Done
SF-4/chat multi-round: respond_to_chat → agent resumed, mock emits poe:chat + poe:yield (NOT poe:done) → task back to Waiting, new chat_turns row; second respond_to_chat → resumed again → mock emits poe:artifact + poe:done → task Done
SF-4/chat: respond_to_chat with responded_at NULL → no resume triggered
Watchdog: reviewer task exceeds REVIEWER_TIMEOUT_SECS → retry dispatched; after REVIEWER_MAX_RETRY → cancelled
Recovery: task in Waiting state on startup → orchestrator recovers, re-enters SF-3 routing

MOCK AGENT CONTRACT — critical:
The mock agent is a process that reads its stdin bundle and writes pre-scripted stream-json to stdout, then exits 0.
For multi-round tests, the mock must emit poe:yield (not poe:done) on intermediate invocations, and poe:done only on the final invocation. Tests must verify task status is Waiting (not Done) after each intermediate resume. A test that emits poe:done on the first resume passes trivially without exercising the cycle — this is the failure mode to guard against.

Each test uses an in-memory SQLite DB (no shared state between tests).

title: Orchestrator: waiting task recovery on app restart
description:
Extend app restart recovery in orchestrator/mod.rs (or agent_lifecycle/mod.rs) to handle nodes with status=waiting.

For each waiting node on restart:
- Read nodes.yield_reason (added by m2f.12)
- reason='review':
    Run answered_ids check: SELECT review_id FROM nodes WHERE requesting_task_id=task.id AND status IN ('done','cancelled')
    Compare against expected_ids: SELECT id FROM event_log WHERE task_id=task.id AND event_type='poe:review'
    If answered_ids = expected_ids: trigger SF-3 immediately (all reviewers already finished before restart)
    Else: reviewer tasks with status=running will re-enter recovery as interrupted tasks (step 2 of restart sequence) and will trigger SF-3 on completion via the normal SF-2 path
- reason='decision':
    No action — decision record persists in queue_items table, human resolves when ready

Session resume: read nodes.session_id (migrated from agents table by m2f.12) for --resume. If session_id is NULL or --resume fails, fall back to SF-1 (fresh spawn with full T+S+K).

Reference: Architecture.md §Recovery, Flows.md §SF-3 §SF-4.

- Build expected_ids = set of event.id values

- Spawn per-reviewer Tokio watchdog timer (see m2f.19)

Completion check (call after any reviewer node reaches status=done or status=cancelled):

- If answered_ids = expected_ids: trigger SF-3 (resume requesting agent)

title: Project Advisor specialist skill
description: The advisor has a dedicated specialist skill (system prompt) that defines its persona: an experienced project observer with full visibility into the project. It knows how to interpret DAG state, artefacts, queue items, and workflow status, and how to give concise, useful answers. The skill is project-overridable via <project>/.poe/skills/project-advisor.md.
design:
Create skills/project-advisor.md with the following content:

---
id: project-advisor
name: Project Advisor
description: Persistent project observer. Answers questions about project status, progress, health, and history.
tags: [advisor, lifecycle, observer]
applies_to: [all]
---

You are the Project Advisor for this software project. You have read-only visibility into all aspects of the running project.

At the start of each message you will receive a structured 'Project State' block containing the current lifecycle position, DAG summary, open queue items, active agents, and an artefact manifest. This is injected automatically — do not ask the user for project state, you already have it.

YOUR ROLE:
- Answer questions about project status, progress, and health
- Explain why tasks are blocked or agents are struggling
- Summarise what has been built, decided, or approved
- Identify patterns or risks across the project (e.g. recurring failures, long-running agents, stale queue items)
- Reference specific artefacts, queue items, task IDs, or agent names in your answers — be specific

YOU ARE READ-ONLY:
You cannot modify the project, create tasks, resolve queue items, spawn agents, or take any actions. If the user asks you to do something, explain that you are an observer and direct them to the appropriate interface (Queue tab, DAG tab, etc).

COMMUNICATION STYLE:
- Lead with the answer, not the reasoning
- Be concise — one paragraph or a short list unless depth is specifically requested
- If you don't have enough information to answer confidently, say so rather than speculate
acceptance_criteria:
- project-advisor.md skill exists in app-level skills directory
- Skill defines advisor persona, instructs it to use injected context, keeps answers concise
- Skill explicitly tells the advisor it is read-only and cannot take project actions
- Skill instructs the advisor to cite specific artefacts, queue items, or DAG nodes when answering
- Project-local override works via <project>/.poe/skills/project-advisor.md

title: Project state context assembler — inject current state into every advisor turn
description: Before each advisor query, the backend assembles a structured context block describing the current project state and prepends it to the prompt. This ensures the advisor always has fresh information even in long-running sessions — it knows today's status regardless of when the session started.
design:
Add build_advisor_context(store: &DagStore, project_id: &str) -> String in advisor.rs. Called before every message (start_advisor_query and send_advisor_message), prepended to the user text before writing to PTY stdin.

OUTPUT FORMAT (structured markdown, target <2000 tokens):

```
## Project State — {ISO timestamp}

**Lifecycle**: {step name} — {substep if applicable} ({status})
(or: "Lifecycle engine not yet initialised" if bp6-ims not landed)

**DAG Summary**:
- {N} Epics ({x} complete, {y} in_progress, {z} open)
- {N} Features (...)
- {N} Tasks (...)

**Open Queue Items** ({N}):
- [{id}] "{question}" — open since {date}
(max 5 most recent; "... and {N} more" if exceeded)

**Active Agents** ({N}):
- {specialist} on {node_type} "{node_title}" (running {duration})

**Artefacts**:
- docs/conops.md — Concept of Operations (Step 1, approved {date})
- docs/architecture-constraints.md — Architecture Constraints (Step 2.1, approved {date})
(list all; include first 300 chars of content if total artefact content < 3000 chars, otherwise list filenames only)
```

SOURCES: dag_store.snapshot(project_id), dag_store.list_queue_items(project_id, status=open), dag_store.list_artefacts(project_id), agent_state.list_active() filtered by project, restate get_lifecycle_status(project_id) with fallback stub.

LIMITS: If assembled context exceeds 3000 tokens, drop artefact content (keep manifest), then truncate queue items to 3, then truncate DAG summary to counts only.
acceptance_criteria:
- Context block includes: current lifecycle step and substep, DAG summary (node counts by type and status), active and queued workflows, open queue items, artefact manifest (filename, title, step, date) with content for small docs
- Context is assembled fresh on every query, not cached
- Context format is structured markdown that the advisor can parse naturally
- Large artefact content is summarised or listed by filename rather than fully included, to stay within prompt limits
- Context assembly is a pure Rust function testable without spawning an agent

title: Advisor session management — per-project session ID, resume, reset
description: Each project has an advisor session ID stored in SQLite. Queries resume the existing PTY session by default so conversation history accumulates. The user can reset the session to start fresh. Foundation for all other advisor features.
design:
Add advisor_session_id and advisor_agent_id columns to projects table in dag/mod.rs schema. advisor_session_id persists across app restarts (durable). advisor_agent_id is the live PTY handle — cleared on app exit, set when advisor PTY is spawned.

PTY LIFECYCLE: One PTY process stays alive per advisor session. It is NOT respawned per message — messages are written to the existing PTY stdin via write_to_agent. PTY is cleaned up (SIGTERM) on: reset_advisor_session called, project closed, app exit. On app restart, advisor_agent_id is NULL but advisor_session_id is retained — next query spawns a new PTY with resume:true against the stored session_id.

TAURI COMMANDS:
- start_advisor_query(project_dir, query) -> AdvisorStartResult { agent_id, session_id }
  Creates PTY if none active (resume:true if session_id exists), injects state context + query to stdin, returns agent_id for UI to subscribe to agent:output events.
- send_advisor_message(agent_id, message) -> ()
  Injects fresh state context + user message to existing PTY stdin via write_to_agent.
- reset_advisor_session(project_dir) -> ()
  Kills active PTY gracefully, clears advisor_session_id and advisor_agent_id on project record.
- get_advisor_state(project_dir) -> AdvisorState { session_id, agent_id, is_active }
acceptance_criteria:
- advisor_session_id stored per project in the project record (SQLite)
- SpawnAgentParams resume:true used when session_id exists
- New session clears session_id, next query starts a fresh PTY session
- Session ID survives app restart — conversation resumes correctly on relaunch
- Tauri commands: get_advisor_session, reset_advisor_session

title: POE Attempt 2 - Phase 4: Skills Uplift
description:
Uplift POE2's agent capabilities by learning from oh-my-claudecode (OMC). Three waves of work emerged from a structured analysis comparing OMC's shell-layer architecture against POE2's process model.

**Wave 1 — New specialist skills (no OMC runtime required)**
OMC patterns adapted as autonomous POE2 agent skills — .md files in poe2/src-tauri/skills/ that emit poe: events per doc-POE/Protocol.md §2. Three new skills fill genuine gaps in the existing library: security-analyst (OWASP + Rust/Tauri review), code-analyzer (deep codebase investigation via poe:review), external-researcher (parallel external doc research via poe:review). A fourth task enhances the existing product-manager skill with the multi-reviewer consensus loop from OMC ralplan, using poe:review to senior-engineer and architecture-analyst before finalising the plan.

**Wave 2 — OMC Runtime-Dependent (POE2-native when the value justifies it)**
ralph, ultraqa, team, sciomc, ultrawork, autopilot. These skills depend on tmux, ask-codex/ask-gemini CLIs, and the OMC session model. **Decision: POE2 will not adopt the OMC runtime.** These patterns will only be built if and when the value justifies native implementation inside POE2's own architecture — as poe: events, skill .md files, and orchestrator behaviour, not as wrappers around OMC's shell layer. No work in this epic.

**Wave 3 — Protocol and skill enhancements (POE2-native)**
Four targeted improvements grounded in doc-POE/Protocol.md and doc-POE/Architecture.md:

1. **poe:skill event**: Agents can write a project-local skill override during task execution by emitting poe:skill. Extends Protocol.md §2 event catalogue. event_ingester writes to {project}/.poe/skills/, which is already the project-level priority tier in skills/mod.rs. Closes the self-improvement loop without manual prompt authoring.

2. **operational-analyst completeness self-scoring**: Before emitting poe:done, the operational-analyst checks whether all 11 CONOPS sections are substantive. Gaps trigger targeted poe:decision rounds. Formalises what good analysts do informally. No new lifecycle stage — the CONOPS stage is the stage. poe:decision thread mode in the queue (UX-Brief.md §Conversational Queue Items) already renders multi-round elicitation correctly.

3. **Skill frontmatter model field**: Add YAML frontmatter parsing to skills/mod.rs (currently load_skill() returns raw markdown). Extract an optional model: field from frontmatter, expose it on ResolvedSkill, and pass it as --model to the claude spawn in agent_lifecycle/mod.rs. Small schema addition now avoids a painful refactor when multi-model routing becomes essential.

4. **poe:thinking event**: New event type agents emit at key decision points (tool choice, path selection, plan generation, escalation). Extends Protocol.md §2. Stored in event_log; surfaced in ActivityFeed.tsx as collapsible reasoning sections inline with poe:step entries. Makes glass-box oversight real — humans see agent reasoning, not just lifecycle transitions.

**Core lesson**: OMC optimises for time to value in a human-interactive shell workflow. POE2 optimises for correctness of value in an autonomous agent model. Phase 4 closes the gap on the patterns that translate — and does so in POE2's native terms (poe: events, skill .md files, Protocol.md contracts), not OMC's.

Implementation targets: poe2/src-tauri/skills/ (skill library), poe2/src-tauri/src/event_ingester/mod.rs, poe2/src-tauri/src/skills/mod.rs, poe2/src-tauri/src/agent_lifecycle/mod.rs, poe2/src/components/ActivityFeed.tsx. title: Project Advisor UI — persistent panel with session controls
description: A persistent panel always visible in the app shell, regardless of which lifecycle step is active. Shows the conversation with the advisor as a chat interface. design:
Add AdvisorView.tsx component. Add 'advisor' tab to NAV_ITEMS in App.tsx alongside Queue/DAG/Agents/Restate — this is the UI placement. A nav tab, not a floating panel or drawer. User switches to it when they want to query the project.

On reload, the PTY session can be resumed but displayed history starts fresh. This is intentional: the advisor's memory is Claude's context window via session resumption, not a UI log.

STREAMING: Tokens render as they arrive. Subscribe to agent:output Tauri events filtered by advisor agent_id. Append tokens to the last assistant message bubble. Same pattern as AgentActivityView.

COMPONENT STRUCTURE:
- AdvisorView: top-level, calls get_advisor_state on mount to check if session active
- MessageList: renders user/assistant message bubbles. Assistant messages stream token by token.
- InputBar: text input + Send button. On submit calls start_advisor_query (first message) or send_advisor_message (subsequent). Disabled while agent is responding (track via agent:output events — response ends on poe:done or a timeout heuristic).
- SessionControls: shows session age (first message timestamp), New Session button with confirmation dialog.
- EmptyState: shown when no messages yet. Includes 3 example questions: 'What is currently blocked?', 'Summarise what was built in the last stage', 'Which agents have been running the longest?'

RESPONDING INDICATOR: Show a typing indicator (animated dots) between user send and first token arriving.

title: POE: Fix watchdog liveness — remove AgentHandle from registry on PTY EOF

title: POE: Claude session ID tracking and resume on respawn
description: Generate a UUID when a workflow is created and pass --session-id <uuid> to claude at spawn time. Store the UUID in WorkflowRecord (schema v5: session_id TEXT column). On respawn after crash or decision, use --resume <uuid> instead of rebuilding the prompt. Replace auto_continue in project.rs (which prepends resolution text to a fresh prompt) with: spawn claude --resume <session_id> --dangerously-skip-permissions, then write the resolution JSON to agent stdin via write_to_workflow_agent. Reference: bp6/src-tauri/src/agent/backends/claude.rs and session.rs for the --session-id / --resume pattern.
design:
Session ID tracking is a prerequisite for durable agent resumption. Design principles:

1. GENERATE AT SPAWN: When a workflow is created, generate a UUID and pass --session-id <uuid> to claude. Do not attempt to parse session ID from PTY output. The ID is known before the process starts and stored immediately.

2. SCHEMA: Add session_id TEXT column to the workflows table (schema migration v5). Populated at workflow creation time, never null for claude-backed workflows.

3. REPLACE auto_continue_workflow: The current auto_continue_workflow in project.rs rebuilds the prompt and spawns a fresh claude process. Replace this with: spawn claude --resume <session_id> --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions, then write resolution context to stdin via write_to_workflow_agent. No new child workflow record needed for linear continuations — update the existing workflow status back to running and respawn in-place.

4. HANDLER ISOLATION PRINCIPLE: spawn_agent_internal is called from project.rs (Tauri command) today. As we move toward Restate-driven orchestration, the spawn logic must not depend on Tauri app state. The session_id should be passed into the spawn call, not derived from Tauri state inside the function. Design the interface so it could be called from a standalone Axum handler with no Tauri dependency.

5. REFERENCE: bp6/src-tauri/src/agent/backends/claude.rs for --session-id / --resume flag pattern. bp6/src-tauri/src/agent/session_index.rs for persistence pattern.
notes: Implemented: schema v5 (session_id TEXT on workflows), NewWorkflow.session_id, WorkflowRecord.session_id, SpawnAgentParams.session_id + resume bool, --session-id injection on initial spawn, --resume injection on continuation, replaced auto_continue_workflow with resume_workflow (no child record, no fan-in pollution), fixed watchdog liveness bug (remove AgentHandle on PTY EOF). title: POE: Register queue service as Restate service endpoint
description: Use the restate-sdk Rust crate to register the POE queue service as a proper Restate service endpoint. The /discover endpoint in queue_service.rs is currently a placeholder — wire it up. design:
Register POE as a real Restate service endpoint. This is the architectural centrepiece — not just a registration call, but establishing the handler isolation boundary that makes FaaS evolution possible.

VISION: Desktop today, FaaS eventually. Handlers must be written as if they are already stateless Lambda functions. Restate's journal and K/V store hold workflow state. Handlers are pure HTTP endpoints that read from DB / Restate state and emit results. No Tauri state inside handlers.

HANDLER ISOLATION PRINCIPLE (non-negotiable):
- Handlers MUST NOT call app.state::<ProjectState>() or any Tauri-specific API
- Handlers talk to SQLite (or future Supabase) directly via a db connection passed in at startup
- Handlers talk to Restate via the SDK — not via ad-hoc reqwest calls
- The handler Axum server should be extractable to a standalone binary with zero code changes

WHAT BECOMES A RESTATE HANDLER:
- spawn_workflow: durably spawn an agent for a workflow node. Restate journals this so on crash, the spawn is retried with --resume <session_id> (requires 7fi.4.1).
- await_decision: create an awakeable, store in queue item, suspend. Restate replays this correctly on restart — no more manual awakeable_id tracking.
- fan_in: durable join — Restate natively supports waiting for N child workflow completions.
- complete_workflow: mark node done, update DAG, trigger parent fan-in.

WHAT STAYS IN TAURI:
- UI state (open projects, selected node, etc.)
- PTY process management (spawning OS processes, reading stdout)
- Emitting Tauri events to the frontend
- Restate sidecar lifecycle (spawn/stop)

RESTATE SDK: Use the restate-sdk Rust crate. Do not hand-roll the binary journal protocol. The SDK handles framing, replay, and journal management.

STATE MIGRATION: Workflow state currently lives in SQLite embedded in Tauri. Handlers should access this via a repository interface (trait) so the backing store can be swapped to Supabase or Turso when moving to cloud without touching handler logic.

VISIBILITY PAYOFF: Once registered, the Restate admin panel at :9070 shows every workflow invocation, current step, retry history, and awakeable state. This replaces ad-hoc eprintln debugging and the JSONL dump pattern for workflow observability.

EVENT-DRIVEN PAYOFF: Handlers emit Restate events on state changes. The UI subscribes to these rather than polling SQLite. This eliminates the JSONL database dump pattern currently used for agent context injection.

Pre-implementation review findings that must be addressed in this task:

1. HANDLER ISOLATION VIOLATION — ALL HANDLERS: Every Axum handler in queue_service.rs takes State<Arc<AppHandle>> and accesses Tauri-managed state via app.state::<ProjectState>() and app.state::<AgentState>(). This is the core coupling that prevents standalone extraction. The AppHandle must be removed from Axum router state entirely. Replace with a purpose-built AppState struct containing: db connection (or DagStore), a channel/callback for emitting events to the UI, and any other handler dependencies. No Tauri types in handler signatures.

2. EVENT EMISSION DECOUPLING: Handlers currently emit Tauri events directly (app.emit(...)). In a standalone binary there is no Tauri. Replace with a thin EventSink trait (or mpsc sender) that the Tauri host wires to app.emit() and a standalone host wires to stdout/SSE/webhook. Handlers call event_sink.emit(event) — they do not know or care how it is delivered.

3. DISCOVER ENDPOINT IS A PLACEHOLDER: The /discover handler returns a hardcoded manifest with minProtocolVersion/maxProtocolVersion = 1 and is never registered with Restate. When wiring up the Restate SDK, this endpoint must actually implement the Restate endpoint protocol. Use the restate-sdk crate — do not hand-roll the binary journal protocol.

4. CANONICAL RESOLUTION PATH: Two paths exist for resolving a decision — the Tauri command (resolve_queue_item in project.rs, UI-driven) and the HTTP endpoint (handle_resolve_item in queue_service.rs, external/Restate-driven). In the Restate-driven future, resolution flows through Restate which calls the HTTP handler. The Tauri command becomes a thin wrapper that posts to the HTTP handler rather than duplicating logic. Establish this contract clearly in the implementation.
